title: Fire Circle & Campfire Experience
strapline: Gathering round a real fire — awe, warmth and story, framed by clear rules that teach respect for genuine risk.
intent: Children experience the awe, warmth and gathering-magic of a real fire, a memorable highlight of forest-school practice.
Children learn to manage genuine risk with respect — the fire circle rules keep everyone safe and are taken seriously.
Children build focus, patience and self-regulation, sitting and waiting their turn in a calm, purposeful ritual.
Children develop a sense of belonging and shared ritual, gathered together around a warm centre.
Children observe real change — wood to flame to ash, water to steam — and the science of heat and burning.
implementation: This is a staff-led, high-supervision activity: only trained adults light and tend the fire, following your forest-school and risk-assessment procedures to the letter.
Teach and rehearse the fire-circle rules every single time: walk round the outside, sit on the log, kneel to enter, and the 'safe distance' line.
Establish clear roles — adults tend the fire, children sit on the seating ring — and never leave a lit fire unsupervised for a moment.
Keep water, a first-aid kit and a fire blanket to hand, and brief every adult on the emergency procedure before you light up.
Build the ritual: gather, light, warm hands, share a story or song, toast something simple, then watch it safely out together.
Talk about what you all see — the colours, the smoke, the change from wood to ash — feeding wonder and early science.
key_questions: What are our fire-circle rules — can you remind everyone?
What colours can you see in the flames?
What is happening to the wood as it burns?
How do we keep ourselves safe near the fire?
How does the warmth feel from here?

impact.text: Children follow important rules and boundaries, understanding they keep everyone safe.
Children sit, wait and focus with patience in a calm shared ritual.
Children explore change and forces — wood to flame to ash, heat, smoke — with fascination.
Children ask real questions about what they see and expect real answers.
Children experience belonging and shared ritual gathered together.

enhancements: Toasting marshmallows or baking bread twists on sticks, following food-safety and allergy checks.
A story or song shared around the fire, building a treasured group ritual.
A 'fire keeper' helper role (age-appropriate, adult-guided) fetching safe kindling from a distance.
Watching the fire safely die down and go cold, examining the ash and charcoal afterwards.
Charcoal mark-making with the cooled remains — drawing with the fire's leftovers.

playing_exploring: Children explore a genuinely new, awe-filled experience with all their senses.
Watching the fire's colours, movement and change captivates deep attention.
active_learning: Children self-regulate and focus to take part safely in something they clearly value.
The specialness of the fire circle motivates real patience and rule-following.
creating_thinking: Children ask questions and reason about heat, burning and change.
They connect the rules to real consequences, understanding why safety matters.
